precepts.text: Herod killed James and jailed Peter; the church prayed in a safe house, and when the angel freed Peter they told the damsel she was mad and that it was his angel, because they thought he was dead and could not visit him. Peter was a fugitive for the rest of his life.
precepts.point: For God is your guide, and the guide of them that keep my commandments; let not your sins weigh you down. We do sin, and if we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves, but if we confess he is faithful to forgive; that is the difference between us and the Christian who teaches sin has no consequences. Let not your iniquities lift up themselves, for woe to them that are bound with their sins, covered as a field with thorns that no man can travel through, left undressed and cast into the fire. When you are bound, there is no magic scripture; you have to want to be released.
precepts.why:
“Hear, O ye my beloved, saith the Lord: behold, the days of trouble are at hand, but I will deliver you from the same. Be ye not afraid neither doubt”. Why neither doubt? Because doubt comes. My mama just got put to death, my children, my wife; Lord, are you going to save us? Remember John the Baptist when he was imprisoned; that little bit of doubt crept in. Acts shows the situation.

“Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword. And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also. (Then were the days of unleavened bread.)” James was beheaded; Peter was in prison. The angel brought Peter out, and he went to “the house of Mary the mother of John, whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together praying.” That was a safe house where Israelites were hiding and praying. When the damsel knew Peter's voice, “they said unto her, Thou art mad”, and “Then said they, It is his angel.”

What did they think had happened to Peter? That he had been put to death. It shows you could not go visit him. There was no visitation, as there are prisons like Guantanamo Bay in Cuba today, with no lawyers and no visitors, and they are building more like it. So do not think, the brothers don't care about me, the sisters didn't come visit me. There will be places nobody can visit you. It is not that we do not care; we cannot get to you. All the saints could do was pray.

And Peter was on the run, a fugitive from the government the rest of his life. The Lord intervened for one and gave him more time, and the other, James, was killed. It is going to get like that, brothers and sisters. That is why we study, pray and apply: knowing ahead of time is supposed to strengthen your resolve, so that you are not afraid, neither doubt.

precepts.text: Herod the king killed James with the sword and, seeing it pleased the Jews, took Peter also. The devil casting into prison was Rome and Herod, Satan's children.
precepts.point: When the Bible says devil, it is interchangeable: the father and his children. His children can do nothing without the spirit in them, the same way we can do nothing without the Lord in us.
precepts.why:
“Behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison”. Did the literal devil come and cast people into prison? Did a spiritual demon snatch somebody and throw him in a cell? No. When the Bible says devil, it is interchangeable: it is talking about the father and his children. The same way we can do nothing without our Father and without the Lord in us, these people can do nothing without their father dwelling in them. He uses his children to do what he wants done.

Acts 12 shows who did it: “Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword. And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also.” Herod was a white man, an Edomite. He killed James and put Peter in prison. So at that time the devil casting into prison was Herod, Satan’s children, Rome.

The seed of the devil came back as Esau, and the sons of God came back as Jacob: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Satan means adversary, accuser, opponent: he is the Lord’s adversary and ours, and so is his seed. Devil means deceiver: as he deceived Eve, his children deceive everyone on the earth. That is why we call the so-called white man the devil, because he deceives the whole earth, and Satan, because he is our adversary and God’s.

So know who we are fighting. This is war, and the devil still casts some of us into prison through his children.

precepts.text: Herod, in royal apparel, gave an oration and the people shouted, It is the voice of a god; immediately the angel of the Lord smote him because he gave not God the glory, and he was eaten of worms. Our people always think the white man is God; God always reminds them.
precepts.point: He still breathed out fire against the Jews; that hatred is bred in them. Then he fell from his chariot, rotted until he could not abide his own smell, and said, It is meet to be subject unto God, and a man that is mortal should not proudly think of himself as if he were God.
precepts.why:
Cyrus the Persian humbled himself and let all Israel go, and God said, you can rule. But the Greek Antiochus “had spoken proudly”, saying “he would come to Jerusalem and make it a common burying place of the Jews.” As soon as he spoke those proud words, “a pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts”, and that most justly, because he had tormented other men’s bowels. He fell from his chariot, rotted until he could not abide his own smell, and finally said “It is meet to be subject unto God, and that a man that is mortal should not proudly think of himself if he were God.”

It did not stop with the Greeks. Now we come down to the Romans, because that is what Herod was: “And upon a set day Herod, arrayed in royal apparel, sat upon his throne, and made an oration unto them. And the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man.”

Black folk always think the white man is God, and God always has to remind you who he is. “And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost.” Antiochus rotted with worms rising out of his body; Herod was eaten of worms. The same judgment for the same pride.

Pride destroyed them. All kingdoms fall because of pride, and nobody is exempt: Assyria, Babylon, Greece, Rome, America. That is the judgment for it. So check yourself before you wreck yourself: a man that is mortal must not think of himself as if he were God.

precepts.why:
Herod stretched out his hands against the church, killed James the brother of John with the sword, and then took Peter because killing James pleased the Jews. Peter was apprehended and put in prison. Herod is the Edomite ruler under Rome. That history shows the devil casting believers into prison and trying them; the warning to Smyrna is something the church had already experienced.

So understand this: this is not any kind of racist rhetoric. This is straight Bible fact.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: And the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man. They said, the way Herod speaks, Herod has got to be a god. That dude can speak very well.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost. God killed him right there. He should have said, nah man, do not put me up as any god. But he was like, yes, I am a god — that speech I did was perfect, you see how I put this word with that word and lowered my voice and carried it up.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: Herod was highly displeased with them of Tyre and Sidon, that is Lebanon, but they came with one accord to him and desired peace. Why? Because their country was nourished by the king's country. It is one verse, but it speaks volumes.

Read from the screen: in 2024 the United States exported a record 5.47 billion dollars in food and agricultural products to the Caribbean basin, a region of 37 countries; the US typically supplies roughly 50 to 55 percent of the region's total food imports. That is Acts 12:20. America makes deals with countries: you are not allowed to grow your own food; we will feed you. So when America says get rid of the Cuban doctors, they all say yes, boss.

Do not forget Bill Clinton. In 2010, as UN special envoy to Haiti, he publicly apologized to the Senate Foreign Relations Committee for forcing Haiti to reduce tariffs on imported US rice during his administration: "It may have been good for some of my farmers in Arkansas, but it has not worked. It was a mistake." He admitted the policy destroyed local Haitian rice production and hindered Haiti's ability to be self-sufficient, and told Democracy Now, "I have to live every day with the consequences of the loss of capacity to produce a rice crop in Haiti to feed those people, because of what I did." The policy led to increased dependency on foreign food aid. After the apology, nothing changed. If you depend on somebody for food and they get mad at you, they cut the supply and your whole country starves. It is all a trick bag.

The third example: Herod killed James with the sword, and because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded to take Peter also. The government attacked the Israelites because it pleased a portion of the very people. Do not think the ones we pass flyers to will not side with the government when it turns on us.

Then were the days of unleavened bread: they waited until the highest holy days to attack. Christ was killed on Passover, and Peter was arrested on Passover. Imagine we get snatched up on Passover, or something happens to the men traveling all over the world for Passover: we want you praying without ceasing, like the church prayed for Peter.

The angel of the Lord came upon him, and a light shined in the prison, and his chains fell off from his hands. The angel walked him past the first and second ward, and the iron gate opened of his own accord, and Peter thought he saw a vision. When Peter was come to himself, he said, Now I know of a surety, that the Lord hath sent his angel, and hath delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews. The government and his own people were against him; all we have is the prayer of the church and the angels answering those prayers.

Herod examined the keepers and commanded that they should be put to death; then on a set day, arrayed in royal apparel on his throne, he made an oration, and the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man. And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost. That is the same spirit as calling a president the savior. God is still listening to these empires talk.
